key_insight: This paper goes beyond 2D appearance matching for cross-view object geo-localization by introducing a geometry-aware, single-stage framework that uses richer spatial cues to better align ground/drone queries with satellite references. It also pairs the model with a large, high-fidelity building dataset to address the lack of geometric metadata and standardized field-of-view imagery.
problem_solved: It addresses cross-view object geo-localization, where an object seen from a ground or drone view must be found in geo-tagged overhead imagery. The paper tackles key bottlenecks in existing methods: overreliance on 2D matching, insufficient datasets with geometry labels, limited prompt diversity, and weak support for standard field-of-view imagery.
method: Introduces a large-scale building dataset with high-fidelity geo-related annotations to support geometry-aware learning.
Proposes a unified single-stage framework designed to directly perform cross-view localization using both appearance and geometric information.
Moves beyond pure 2D correspondence by incorporating spatial structure for more robust matching across drastically different viewpoints.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work suggests a more scalable and accurate direction for cross-view localization by combining data quality with geometry-aware modeling. It is especially relevant for robotics, remote sensing, urban mapping, and any application needing reliable localization across viewpoint gaps.

paper_title: Beyond 2D Matching: A Unified Single-Stage Framework for Geometry-Aware Cross-View Object Geo-Localization
paper_authors: Liyao Wang, Ruipu Wu, Haojun Xu, Lei Shi, Linjiang Huang
